tagline: Down the Delaware Bay through the marsh towns to Cape May.
intro: From Mannington Township the byway runs down through Salem and along the Delaware Bay, sometimes skimming the shoreline, sometimes moving inland over the Cohansey and Maurice rivers and through farmland and old villages, 122 miles to Cape May Point at the southern tip of New Jersey. Spurs go out to Fort Mott, to Fortescue in its marshes, to Bivalve at Port Norris and to the Lewes ferry.

The shore is mostly wetland, salt marsh and mud flat, and the towns lived on what came out of it: oysters and caviar, crabs and salt hay. The bay holds the largest population of spawning horseshoe crabs in the world.

moments.title: Greenwich
moments.text: On the tidal Cohansey, tea bound for Philadelphia was taken from a cellar and burned in December 1774, and after the war the town began saying Green-witch, to tell itself from England's.

moments.title: East Point Light
moments.text: The 1849 lighthouse at the mouth of the Maurice River now stands about 40 yards from the water, behind sandbags, on a beach that aerial photos from 1940 show four times as wide.

moments.title: Cape May Point State Park
moments.text: At the end of the road, birds bound south in the fall gather to wait for a favorable wind across the bay, and a half-mile boardwalk trail has several observation platforms.
